questions.q: In the Ising model, what values can a spin variable s_i take?
questions.explain: Ising spin variables take the values +1 (spin up) or -1 (spin down), unlike QUBO's binary variables which take 0 or 1.

questions.q: What is the substitution that converts a QUBO binary variable x_i into an Ising spin s_i?
questions.explain: The standard substitution is s_i = 1 - 2x_i: when x_i = 0, s_i = 1; when x_i = 1, s_i = -1.

questions.q: For the QUBO f(x1,x2) = -5x1 - 3x2 + 2x1x2, converting to Ising form gives H(s1,s2) = -3.5 + 2s1 + s2 + 0.5*s1*s2. What is H(s1,s2) when s1=-1 and s2=-1 (i.e. x1=1, x2=1)?
Why does quantum hardware (annealers, and QAOA's cost Hamiltonian) operate natively in the Ising formulation rather than the QUBO formulation?
options: Because a qubit's Pauli-Z eigenvalues are exactly +1 and -1, matching Ising spin values -- so the physics of the hardware directly implements spin energy, not 0/1 binary cost
Because QUBO cannot be converted into Ising form for most problems
Because Ising Hamiltonians are always simpler to compute by hand than QUBOs
Because quantum hardware cannot represent the number zero
questions.explain: A qubit's Z-eigenvalues are +1 and -1, the same two values an Ising spin takes -- which is precisely why quantum hardware is built to minimize Ising energy, and why every QUBO must be translated into Ising form before it can run on that hardware.

questions.q: What happens to the location of the optimal solution when a QUBO is converted into its equivalent Ising Hamiltonian?
options: The optimal solution's underlying choice stays exactly the same; only its coordinate representation changes from 0/1 to +1/-1
The optimum always shifts to a different variable assignment
The minimum value always becomes zero after conversion
Ising conversion is only valid for QUBOs with a single variable
questions.explain: As the worked example shows, the minimum value and the underlying optimal choice (x=(1,1), i.e. s=(-1,-1)) are identical before and after conversion -- the substitution only relabels the coordinate system, it doesn't change the optimization landscape.
